link_coverage.exhausted_reason: Zero qualifying public issuers, and this is the census that overturned the chain. The chain's example_tickers for this link were IDXX, NEOG, TMO, DHR and ZTS on the reasoning that these are the listed vendors of veterinary and food-safety diagnostics. Tested against the SEC's own full-text index: of the 69 10-K filings that mention "avian influenza", across 48 distinct issuers, NOT ONE is IDEXX, Neogen, Thermo Fisher or Danaher. Zoetis appears, but as a vaccine maker, and it is placed on link 5 where its role actually is. So no US-listed diagnostics company discloses avian influenza as a business exposure at all. The link is real and the testing volume is real; the listed vendors simply do not consider it material enough to write down, which is a stronger statement about this link's investability than any absence of coverage would have been.

research_denominators.note: Six of ten links censused. The four money-corner and middle links asked for on 2026-09-11 (2, 5, 8, 9) joined links 4 and 10 from 2026-09-10. Links 1, 3, 6 and 7 remain OPEN by design: link 1 has no commercial counterparty at all, and links 3, 6 and 7 were not in scope for this pass.
research_denominators.disclosing_population: SEC EDGAR full-text search for "avian influenza" across all US public filers' 10-K filings returns 69 hits across 48 distinct issuers. That is the denominator every middle-link census below is scored against.

notes.text: The census changed the answer and that is the point of running it. Before it, the chain and the impact appraisal both said the poultry-genetics link had no listed exposure at all. The registry search found Cobb-Vantress in the SEC index, and the full-text search found it named in Tyson's own EX-21. So the honest statement is not 'no listed exposure' but 'exactly one listed route, reached through a wholly-owned subsidiary inside a meat processor'. That is a weaker claim and a truer one, and the chain's map_limitation and the appraisal's public_reach rationale should be read against it.

Control probe, run on the same plane and the same query shape as every target search: cal-maine returns CAL-MAINE FOODS INC, CIK 0000016160, SIC 0200 AGRICULTURE PRODUCTION, and charles river returns its filer record. Both are poultry-or-avian-adjacent names of the same specificity as the targets. Non-zero hits on the controls beside zero hits on the targets is what separates a genuine absence from a broken query.
Author run. Status stays ACTIVE and the author does not mark this mapping COMPLETE; that is the fresh-context audit's call, not this seat's.

The middle-link census overturned the chain a second time, on the same shape as the Cobb-Vantress correction. The chain listed IDXX, NEOG, TMO and DHR as the diagnostics link's example_tickers. SEC EDGAR full-text search returns 69 10-K filings mentioning "avian influenza" across 48 distinct issuers, and NOT ONE of those four appears. No US-listed diagnostics company discloses this occurrence as a business exposure, so the link closes EXHAUSTED at zero and the chain's ticker list for it was wrong. The 69-filing population is now the denominator for every middle link and is recorded in research_denominators.

Limit of the disclosing-population method, stated so it is not over-read: the full-text search covers form 10-K only. GSK plc (CIK 0001131399) and Sanofi (CIK 0001121404) file 20-F, and CSL is ASX-listed with no SEC filing, so their ABSENCE from the 69 hits is an artefact of the form filter and is not evidence about them. They hold BARDA pre-pandemic H5 awards and belong to link 10's countermeasure role; identity evidence proving their exchange and ticker was queued rather than asserted, and link 10's coverage is unchanged until it lands. Two further disclosing issuers, PURE Bioscience and TOMI Environmental Solutions, name avian influenza and sit on link 3's biosecurity plane, which this pass did not census; both are deferred to the backlog rather than placed.

CSL, GSK and SNY were pulled for this pass and are NOT placed, which is recorded rather than left as a silent omission. All three hold BARDA pre-pandemic H5 awards, so their role on link 10 is evidenced; what is missing is identity. GSK and Sanofi file 20-F, so the 8-K earnings route that gave every US issuer here its legal-issuer-exchange-ticker span is empty for them, and the EDGAR company pages give legal issuer and CIK but no exchange. CSL is ASX listed and its ASX page renders as a client-side shell carrying only the title. A placement needs all three facts, so they wait. Their market files ARE on disk and usable: CSL-AX sits at 58 per cent of its own 52-week range and CSLLY at 71, against SNY at 13 and GSK at 40. Deferred to the backlog.
